decisions.question: At a loop's pick-up, should a Talus with the loading grab gather only what lies within the grab's reach of where it stops?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.299.0 (row 538): it lifts what its Gather what allows within reach, then leaves once loaded; with nothing in reach it waits the stop's hour for colonists.

options.label: Within reach only
options.detail: As built: put the pick-up beside the pile

options.label: Drive about the pick-up
options.detail: It drives to each thing near the stop, as a gathering run does, until full

decisions.why: Simple and cheap to run; the pick-up is yours to place beside the pile

decisions.question: At a loop's drop-off, should a tipper tip everything aboard?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.299.0: it tips the whole load into the bunker or stockpile the stop is on, or onto the ground; what storage will not take stays aboard.

options.label: Everything aboard
options.detail: As built

options.label: Only what its Gather what allows
options.detail: Anything else (fuel cans, kit) stays aboard

decisions.why: A haul truck's load is whatever was put in it at the pick-up

decisions.question: When should a radio station with remote gun turrets call a colonist to its console?
decisions.context: Built in Radio 0.18.0: only while enemies are about, so nobody sits at the console all day; a turret fires only while watched, so it cannot fire at the first moment of a raid until the operator arrives.

options.label: While enemies are about
options.detail: As built

options.label: Always
options.detail: A colonist sits at the console whenever a turret is on its coax, ready at once

decisions.why: A colonist kept at a console all day is a colonist lost to every other job

decisions.question: An aircraft on a round flies a leg only with the fuel for it and a sixth to spare. Is a sixth right?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.307.0 (rows 549-550), as the airdrop's way home. Short of it, it waits at the stop until refuelled. Vehicle Framework's own figure for the leg is its burn at cruise; our cruise height and engine model change it on the way.

options.label: A sixth more (1.15)
options.detail: As built

options.label: A quarter more (1.25)
options.detail: Safer against headwinds of our own model; shorter legs

options.label: Exactly the leg's fuel
options.detail: Longest legs; a leg that burns more than planned ends on open ground

decisions.why: The same margin as the airdrop's way home, so one rule holds for both

decisions.question: At a loop's drop-off, when nothing takes a tanker's load, should it keep pumping until its hour is up?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.303.0 (row 545): it says so once, keeps its pump running in case room is made (a tower drawn down, a tank emptied), and drives on at the hour's end; emptied, it leaves at once.

options.label: Keep pumping its hour
options.detail: As built; the stop's time is the same as for colonists

options.label: Drive on at once
options.detail: Takes its load back to the pick-up and round again

decisions.why: A tower in use drains while it waits, and an hour lost is cheaper than a load driven round for nothing

decisions.question: Parachute drift on the map is the US Army's real formula scaled to a fifth (real drift would cross most of a map). Keep a fifth?
decisions.context: docs/development/airdrop.md, 'What drops, and how'. 240 m of real drift (1,000 ft in 8 kt) shows as about 32 cells.

options.label: A fifth (0.2)
options.detail: As built

options.label: A tenth (0.1)
options.detail: Loads land closer to the point; the wind matters less

options.label: A third (0.33)
options.detail: The wind matters more; strong wind can carry loads off the map

decisions.why: Drift you can see and plan around without losing loads off a normal map

decisions.question: A parachute's fall on the map takes half its real time (a 1,000 ft jump: 52 s real, about 26 s). Keep half?
decisions.context: docs/development/airdrop.md. Longer falls leave loads exposed to fire and CIWS for longer.

options.label: Half (0.5)
options.detail: As built

options.label: Real time (1.0)
options.detail: Slower, more exposed to fire

options.label: A quarter (0.25)
options.detail: Quicker drops

decisions.why: RimWorld's time runs faster than real; half keeps a drop watchable without dragging

decisions.question: The Osprey's hold takes one vehicle up to 2 x 3 cells and 2,500 kg. Keep it?
decisions.context: The real V-22 carries only the small Internally Transportable Vehicle. In your game this fits the Wiesel, VVE's Prowler, Dirtbike and Charley, and RimThunder's bicycle; most of your fleet is 2 x 4 or bigger.

options.label: 2 x 3, 2,500 kg
options.detail: As built, near the real cabin

options.label: 2 x 4, 3,500 kg
options.detail: Also VVE's cars and the L-ATV, past the real cabin's size

decisions.why: Realism: the C-27J is the vehicle carrier

decisions.question: InterRim Ballistic Missile's CIWS does 4 points of bullet damage to an enemy aircraft per hit it rolls. Keep 4?
decisions.context: IRBM rolls a hit most ticks it fires, so this brings an Osprey down in well under a minute of fire.

options.detail: As built
Aircraft survive a pass more often
A CIWS is deadly to anything crossing

decisions.why: Authored; no figure fits IRBM's per-tick roll
